questions.title: Two Sum
questions.prompt: Solve Two Sum. Talk through your approach before coding, then implement it in the editor.
questions.answerOutline: Strong candidates state the brute force, then improve it with a single-pass hash map, explaining why checking before inserting avoids reusing an element. They test with duplicates ([3,3], target 6) and negative numbers.
commonMistakes: Inserting before checking, so the same index is used twice
Sorting and losing the original indices
followUps: What if the array is sorted? (two pointers, O(1) space)
What if you need all unique pairs?
What if the input doesn't fit in memory?
questions.rubricNotes: 5: optimal solution, clean code, tests edge cases unprompted. 3: reaches the hash map approach with hints. 1: stuck at brute force or code doesn't handle the basics.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.prompt: Merge all overlapping intervals. Explain how you decide whether two intervals overlap.
expectedConcepts: Single pass merging with the last interval
Use max for the end to handle containment
questions.answerOutline: Sort by start, then merge in one pass. Touching intervals ([1,4],[4,5]) count as overlapping. Uses max(end) for containment cases.
followUps: Insert a new interval into an already-merged list in O(n)
Minimum meeting rooms needed (heap or sweep line)
questions.rubricNotes: Look for a clear overlap definition before coding, and tested edge cases.

questions.title: LRU Cache
questions.prompt: Design and implement an LRU cache with O(1) get and put.
expectedConcepts: Doubly linked list for recency order
Eviction removes from the map and the list
questions.answerOutline: Explain why a map alone can't track order and a list alone can't find nodes. Implement move-to-front and evict-tail. Mention LinkedHashMap access order as a library shortcut.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to remove the evicted key from the map
O(n) removal from a singly linked list
questions.rubricNotes: Strong candidates draw the structure first and handle pointer updates carefully.

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.prompt: Count the islands in a grid. Discuss DFS vs BFS.
questions.answerOutline: Scan the cells and flood-fill each new island. Mention the stack overflow risk of recursive DFS on large grids, and Union-Find as an alternative.
commonMistakes: Not marking cells visited, causing infinite loops
Out-of-bounds checks in the wrong order
followUps: The grid is streamed row by row
questions.rubricNotes: Reward clean neighbour iteration and explicit complexity analysis.
